What are the types of forces?

Contact forces, non-contact forces, and the difference between weight and mass

Can a force be exerted on an object without any physical contact?

  • Describe gravitational force and magnetic force.
  • State the differences between weight and mass, and give the SI unit of each.

Core concept

What is friction and where does it act?

Friction acts wherever two surfaces touch, and ALWAYS against the motion.

Learn
  • An object or a body can exert a force on another object or body through physical contact. Forces acting between two objects that are in physical contact with each other are called contact forces.If the two things are touching, the force between them is a contact force. That is the whole test.
  • Friction is the force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact.
  • It is the force that allows us to hold on to things without dropping them.Without friction a glass would slide straight out of your fingers, however hard you squeezed.
Key Facts
  • Friction is a contact force: the two surfaces must be touching.
  • Friction always opposes motion. It never drives an object forward on its own.
  • A rougher surface gives more friction than a smoother one.
Test

A climber rubs chalk on his hands. Why does this help him grip?

📓Now complete your notes: Section A: Contact forcesFill the two blanks in the friction Take Note! box. Use the exact words from the Learn tab.
Core concept

What is elastic force?

Stretch or squash an elastic object and it actually pushes back the other way!

Learn
  • When an elastic material is stretched or compressed, it resists the change in shape by exerting a force in the opposite direction.Pull a rubber band and you can feel it pulling back. Squash a spring and you can feel it pushing back.
  • Elastic force is the force acting on a stretched or compressed elastic object to return it to its original shape.
  • When a climber falls, the rope stretches and the elastic force exerted increases. This reduces the impact felt by the climber when he falls.A rope that stretches slows the fall over a longer time, so the jolt he feels is smaller than a rope that did not stretch at all.
Key Facts
  • Elastic force is a contact force: the object exerting it is touching what it acts on.
  • The elastic force acts in the opposite direction to the stretch or the squash.
  • A rope that stretches reduces the impact felt by a falling climber.
Test

Why do climbing ropes reduce the impact a climber feels in a fall?

Core concept

Non-Contact Force (Gravitational Force)

Gravity attracts two objects towards one another without the objects touching

Learn
  • Forces acting between two objects that are not touching each other are called non-contact forces. Two types of non-contact forces are gravitational force and magnetic force.
  • Gravitational force is a force that attracts two objects towards each other.
  • When a planet exerts gravitational force on an object and pulls it towards its centre, the object is known to have weight.Weight is not a thing an object owns. It is the size of the pull a planet is giving it right now.
  • Earth's gravitational force pulls all things towards its centre. Skydivers from the Red Lions fall from a height of more than 3000 metres, and gravitational force pulls them down towards Earth's surface.
Key Facts
  • A non-contact force acts between two objects that are not touching.
  • Weight is the measure of the gravitational force acting on an object.
  • Gravitational force also acts on volcanic ash and on falling rain.
Test

Which of these is a non-contact force?

📓Now complete your notes: Section D: Gravitational force and weightFill the three blanks in the Take Note! box. Use the exact words from the Learn tab.
Core concept

Non-Contact Force (Magnetic Force)

Like poles push apart, unlike poles pull together, and neither of them has to touch!

Learn
  • Magnetic force is the force exerted between a magnet and another magnetic material such as iron or steel. Magnetic force also exists between two magnets.
  • Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole. When unlike poles are brought close to each other, they pull together due to the magnetic force of attraction.
  • When like poles are brought close to each other, they push apart due to the magnetic force of repulsion.Two north poles will not stay together. Push them at each other and you can feel them shoving back.
Key Facts
  • Magnetic force acts between a magnet and a magnetic material such as iron or steel.
  • Unlike poles attract. Like poles repel.
  • Magnetic force is a non-contact force: the magnets do not have to touch.
Test

Two bar magnets are brought close and push each other apart. What must be true?

Core concept

Weight vs Mass?

One is a force and changes with location. The other is an amount of matter and does not!

Learn
  • Weight is the measure of the gravitational force acting on an object. As weight is a type of force, the SI unit of weight is the newton (N).
  • Mass is the amount of matter in an object. The SI unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).Mass counts how much stuff there is. Moving the stuff somewhere else does not add to it or take any away.
  • The amount or quantity of matter does not change regardless of location, so the mass of an object remains the same. The weight of an object depends on the gravitational force exerted on the object, which may change with its location.
  • In everyday language the kilogram is commonly used as the unit of weight. In science we make a clear distinction, so 10 kilograms of rice scientifically refers to the mass of rice, instead of its weight.A supermarket label saying ten kilograms is telling you the mass, even though people say weight out loud.
Key Facts
  • Weight is measured with a spring balance. Mass is measured with an electronic balance or a beam balance.
  • Mass remains constant regardless of location. Weight may change with location.
  • A 10 kg bag of rice has a mass of 10 kg on Earth and on the moon, but a weight of 100 N on Earth and 16 N on the moon.
Test

A 10 kg bag of rice is taken to the moon. What happens to it?
